study.question: Does adding the committed g3 private content-plus-linear task readout to the complete g0 memory-joint/collapsed representation exceed BOTH frozen source bests, especially validation four-task macro AUC 0.8303789178781177, at justified parameter and measured compute cost; and can gains be distinguished from shared scorer/content capacity?
study.hypothesis: Observation: g0 macro AUC 0.8303789178781177 exceeds g3 0.8294837888998853, yet g3 cart AUC 0.8682555509294122 exceeds g0 0.8678403944138925 by 0.0004151565155197. Other task AUCs favor g0. Implementation inspection shows g0 adds feedback-conditioned memory before joint token interaction but shares the direct DIN sum across heads, whereas g3 adds task-private content and rank summaries directly to each head. These paths may preserve complementary information. Append the exact g3 readout to g0 without changing g0 summaries or information flow; retain original direct C_t plus shared zero-initialized P(M_t). Shared ancestry may make the new branch redundant or cause gradient interference. This is an integration hypothesis, not a performance, novelty, or confirmed-mechanism claim.

SHA256-matched full imported source inspected. Exact shared action-aware 400->64 task trunk, four private 32-unit scorer heads, C_t+P(M_t) pooling and RNG-fork/zero-output initialization inherited. Replace its older shared representation with the complete stronger g0 memory representation. No new task-conditioning mechanism claimed.

Archived original primary text inspected at lines 250-274: target-aware unnormalized local-activation sum is inherited through both local sources. Added feedback memory, relation/rank tokens and task readouts are local adaptations, not original DIN reproductions.

Pinned benchmark implementation inspected at lines 123-273: task-mask pooled sequence hubs, repeated aggregation/broadcast and mask-free SDPA over zeroed sequence K/V. Candidate instead retains strictly masked compact g0 memory read before one token block and appends g3 output-level residual summaries. No INFNet source or mask-free attention is copied.

Read full authorized section2.3 primary benchmark description. Hub-based layer-wise task/sequence exchange is related, but the proposed study is local source integration with a routing/basis replacement factorial, not a new unified architecture priority claim.

inherited_components: Entire g0 source architecture/configuration at SHA256 20e3a3378483d39cea5679650a73e3ce829a53f988a52f910bfcd5209c7b1cf0; same sanitization, visible history/task-mask semantics, static embeddings, relation counts/content/moments/banks, factorized feedback path, joint/collapsed memory, JointBlock and towers.

Task scorer, task content-plus-extra pooling, projection, gradient policy and initialization from g3 source SHA256 77c0d1afc63e2ffdc4730c0c333eb4b6eeae8260b4b16678535218a6c9074cdf. _task_pool and _moment_coefficients are AST-identical to g3; optional basis argument leaves g0 default linear arithmetic intact.

Frozen host data, labels, optimizers, training pass, dense clipping, scoring and validation selection. No loss hook, new input, future timestamp, current label, user identifier or history visibility change.
study.proposed_difference: Each head now receives [raw static fields, g0 global DIN sum + C_t + P(M_t), g0 interacted token flattening, fixed log counts]. C_t and M_t use g3 residual task scores from target/history item interactions and historical actions. Full g0 memory and all shared token paths execute unchanged. Two-by-two controls substitute FP32 mean scores for private routing and duplicate content C_t for the extra rank M_t. All four own the same active scorer/projection capacity and execute the same operator shapes; copy is an active content-capacity replacement, not a dormant-parameter control. Both sources are mandatory empirical comparators. This design does not factorially switch the full g0 memory bundle off and cannot establish memory-task super-additivity.
predictions: Primary: private_linear will exceed BOTH source macro AUCs on full May12 validation under the fixed recipe; any improvement is preliminary until paired repetitions. Selection never drops a task; ties use macro Logloss, then parameters, then trial ID.

If routing matters on the g0 representation, private_linear exceeds mean_linear and/or private_copy exceeds mean_copy in paired contrasts. If the new rank information matters, linear exceeds copy at fixed routing. Interpret the predeclared interaction separately from these simple effects.

All four have identical parameter counts; added dense estimate 46852 (about 0.142% of g0 total, 3.81% of g0 dense). Extra scoring work grows with B*L, so measured training cost can increase materially despite a small parameter increment. No efficiency improvement is predicted from parameter count alone.

At initialization all four must reproduce g0 predictions because task-score outputs and P are zero and inherited RNG is preserved. Empty-history task residuals stay zero. These are prospective host invariants, not results from local model execution.

Exploratory history slices use existing predeclared empty/1-16/17-64/>64 bins with sample/positive/negative counts. Existing g3 versus g0 macro deltas vary by slice, but do not prove complementary per-example errors. No new bin selection or veto threshold follows from the same validation outcomes.

Validation selection considers all four arms and the frozen sources with the same macro-AUC policy; a control can be the best supported artifact. If mean or copy wins, retain it only with the corresponding restricted content/capacity interpretation, without attributing its gain to private routing or extra rank.
falsifiers: private_linear does not exceed the stronger g0 source, or gain over one source is lost against the other: the proposed combination is unsupported under this recipe.
Mean routing or copy content matches/exceeds private_linear at matched parameters/operators: gains cannot be attributed uniquely to private task routing or added rank information, respectively.
A private_linear gain vanishes/reverses across paired seeds or is reproduced by an active matched control: do not claim repeated mechanism support.

Masked inputs or current target action change predictions; initial g0 function/RNG is not preserved; numerical nonfiniteness, unregistered trainable parameters, OOM or trial-cap overrun occur: execution/integrity failure, not scientific counterevidence against task conditioning.
Added measured cost yields a dominated quality/cost trade-off: do not claim justified efficiency even if macro AUC rises. No hidden per-task veto is introduced.
alternative_explanations: Extra scorer parameters, action-aware relevance, shared content reparameterization, delayed branch learning or optimizer dynamics may explain improvement without a new information mechanism; mean/copy controls address subsets of this ambiguity.

Both imported sources share embeddings/target-aware summaries and linear rank ancestry. Apparent complementarity may be redundant; stronger g0 representations may amplify interference from task gradients.

Source bests are selected single-seed validation records. Selection noise, rare auxiliary positives and repeated user exposures may explain small differences; do not use impression-independent significance tests.

Auxiliary labels match user/category/brand within 24h rather than ad-specific conversions. The frozen official_offline feedback may not be mature at real prediction time; production point-in-time claims are unsupported.

Only three admitted trial IDs exist. Scoped-memory searches returned no matches. Task text mentions unsuccessful older mean/copy trajectories, but their receipts are not supplied in this phase and are not promoted to local negative evidence; new controls remain necessary.

No raw parquets, loader execution, torch, numpy or host execution interface is exposed here. Dataset/loader integrity is inherited from the frozen host contract and source hashes, not independently reverified locally. Missing execution dependencies are not null model results.
